messages:
Raj: quick thought — should we allow a single API key to be used across multiple projects/orgs for partner integrations? easy onboarding but worrying about quota/billing and blast radius. anyone seen a clean model?

Lina: i'm leaning toward not by default. two patterns we've used elsewhere:
1) scoped key: bind at creation to one or a small set of project ids (explicit).
2) delegation token: partner holds a long-lived onboarding key, calls our exchange endpoint to mint short-lived project-bound tokens on behalf of a project.

Dave: agree. scoped keys make attribution/billing/telemetry simple. if we do delegation exchange we must record provenance at mint time and store a mapping for audit. also need to surface which project actually consumed quota in dashboards.

Megan: quota note — default charging should be to the effective_consuming_project (the project id in provenance). allow an admin override at key-creation to bill to a different project/org but that should be explicit and require owner consent.

Raj: can we do a pragmatic migration for legacy keys that currently are used across teams? build an exchange endpoint that returns a project-scoped token when you present the legacy key + a project claim. we can tighten rollout by accepting legacy keys only from a small % initially.

Lina: console UX: when someone creates a cross-project or org-scoped key, show a clear modal: "Who will be billed?" with ripple checkbox "Allow other projects to use this key (requires explicit acceptance)". also add an action to rotate/limit to specific projects later.

Dave: telemetry implications — we should emit these fields on every request: `x-redwood-origin: project:<id>`, `x-redwood-actor: svc:<id>`, and `x-key-id: <key>`. but we MUST avoid exploding cardinality in our metrics. so in metrics pipeline keep numeric ids as tags only for traces; roll up for dashboards to derived dimensions like `billing_project`, `key_scope_type` (scoped/org/delegation).

Megan: agree on rollups. sampling rules: full traces for errors and for requests that change billing/limits, 0.1% sampling for good requests. also add a telemetry gauge for "unattributed_calls" so we can catch requests that miss origin headers.

Raj: security edge-case: partner tries to mint tokens for projects they don't control. exchange endpoint must validate caller context (e.g., signed claim + project owner consent), otherwise reject. keep audit log entry for each mint.

Lina: rollout suggestion: phase 1 — console + API accept new headers (no enforcement), collect telemetry and show `effective_billing_project` column in billing dashboard. phase 2 — opt-in enforcement for some orgs (canary). phase 3 — default enforcement for all new keys, with migration tools for legacy keys.

Dave: small engineering note: implement enforcement as a request middleware that decides `billing_project` and sets a token-scoped RBAC context. middleware also needs an allowlist for cross-project keys for org admins.

Megan: also push a migration checklist for customers: list legacy keys with active usage, recommend creating per-project keys, show traffic delta after cutover. we should provide a one-click proxy-exchange in console for big partners.

Raj: +1. can we make a minimal proto for the exchange API now? something like:

```
POST /v1/token/exchange
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <legacy-key>
Body: { "target_project": "proj_123", "requested_ttl": 3600, "consent_proof": "<signed-consent>" }
Response: { "access_token": "tok_..", "expires_in": 3600, "billing_project": "proj_123" }
```

Lina: that looks fine. require `consent_proof` when target_project != owner_of(legacy-key). consent_proof can be a signed statement from project owner (we'll provide a console action to generate).

Dave: implementation detail — store exchange events in audit logs + create a `key_lineage` document for each minted token. this helps for postmortem/forensics.

Megan: ops — we should also add an SLO for exchange endpoint latency and rate-limit by legacy-key to prevent abuse.

Raj: ok next steps: Lina to prototype console modal and add `effective_billing_project` column to billing dashboard (canary). Dave to sketch middleware and exchange endpoint. Megan to write migration checklist and sampling rules. I'll open a ticket grouping these.

auth-bot: created ticket TICK-4389: "cross-project key exchange + billing attribution plan" and added labels: infra/auth, telemetry, console, rollout.

Lina: cool — i'll drop a rough mock in #design after lunch :thumbsup:

Dave: putting a pointer in the weekly eng sync agenda so we can get quick alignment.

Megan: thanks all, i'll draft the migration email/FAQ.
